=== a chat calls edit_notes
chat: edit_notes {"heading":"Facts","text":"The user wants it fast."}
refusal:
The notes are the orchestrator's own memory, so a chat does not write them. To pass something on, use tell_orchestrator; to change the work, change the tasks.

=== the heading is empty
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":" ## ","text":"x"}
refusal:
the heading is empty

=== no heading given
orchestrator: edit_notes {"text":"x"}
refusal:
the heading is empty

=== nothing to remove: there are no notes
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"Facts","text":""}
refusal:
the notes have no section called 'Facts'; there is nothing to remove

=== added: the first version of the notes
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"Facts","text":"The old importer reads CSV in three passes (T01).\n"}
answer:
Section 'Facts' added; the notes are 59 characters (version 1).

=== added at the end, the heading given with its marks
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"### Sources ","text":"T01."}
answer:
Section '### Sources' added; the notes are 78 characters (version 2).

=== added: a second section
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"Plan","text":"Build it, then measure."}
answer:
Section 'Plan' added; the notes are 112 characters (version 3).

=== replaced: the name in another case, its inner section goes with it
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"  facts","text":"One pass is enough (T02)."}
answer:
Section 'facts' replaced; the notes are 69 characters (version 4).

=== no text given
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"Plan"}
refusal:
text is missing: give the section's new content, or an empty text to remove it

=== removed: the text is empty
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"Plan","text":"  "}
answer:
Section 'Plan' removed; the notes are 35 characters (version 5).

=== nothing to remove
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"Plan","text":"  "}
refusal:
the notes have no section called 'Plan'; there is nothing to remove

=== removing the only section
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"Facts","text":""}
refusal:
removing it would leave the notes empty; replace them with set_notes instead

=== the notes now (version 5)
## Facts

One pass is enough (T02).

=== two sections of that name
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"Facts","text":"Three."}
refusal:
the notes have 2 sections called 'Facts'; rename them with set_notes

=== replaced, the notes are over 20,000 characters
orchestrator: edit_notes {"heading":"Plan","text": 400 lines}
answer:
Section 'Plan' replaced; the notes are 21,240 characters (version 7). They are over 20,000 characters, and every instance reads all of them: shorten them, keeping what the next instance needs to decide.
